page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6.3xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the KVM hypervisor. It runs on an Intel Xeon Platinum 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz across an x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 12 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 6 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The system is provisioned with 48.0 GB of memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include support for AVX-512 vector extensions and VNNI instructions. There is no bundled local storage or integrated GPU, necessitating reliance on network-attached block storage, while baseline network throughput is rated at 4 Gbps.

Benchmark assessments show consistent middle-tier multi-threaded compute and memory bandwidth capabilities, evidenced by a PassMark CPU score of 11955.1 and a Geekbench multi-core rating of 5870.0. Memory throughput yields 71.48 GB/sec on uncached 256 MB reads and 43.18 GB/sec on writes. However, single-threaded metrics indicate noticeable constraints, with stress-ng single-core performance (1311.98) and single-threaded gzip compression (22.79 GB/sec) both falling into the lower quartile. In contrast, parallelized tasks such as Clang compilation (9554.0) and multi-threaded decompression handle concurrent workloads reliably.

Because it features a balanced memory allocation and steady multi-threaded execution, the instance is operationally efficient for mid-tier enterprise microservices, static web traffic handling (measured at 9.06 GB/sec throughput), and in-memory key-value data stores such as Redis, which reached 10.32 million SET operations per second. It is well-fitted for staging environments, container orchestration worker nodes, and production relational databases that do not require ultra-low-latency local NVMe drives.
